summary: Yukio Sakamoto was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Taiken Kimura, Daito Shimaji, and Nichien Fukami. He held professorships at Toyo University and Rissho University, where he also served as dean and president.

Yukio Takeda was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1962). He held academic posts at Hokkaido University (~1964–1968), Nagoya City University (~1968–1978), the University of Tokyo (~1978–1995), and Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (~1998–2005).

Yukio Yamanaka is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied as a graduate student at Kyoto University (attested 1996). He later served as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen (attested 2015).
Yuko Kamishima is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Tokyo and conducted research under Ekai Kawaguchi, later holding a post at Ritsumeikan University.

Yuko Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College. She taught Catherine Ludvik and held a post at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2001).

Yuko Yokochi is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Groningen under Minoru Hara, Katsuhiko Kamimura, and Hans T. Bakker. She served as associate professor (attested 2002) and professor (attested 2012–2021) at Kyoto University.
Yulian Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2010).

Yumi Katayama is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who pursued doctoral studies at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) and studied under supervisor Kenyu Mitomo (attested 2013).

Yumi Nakamoto is a Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2014). She also served as an open-recruitment researcher (2012) and graduate research student (attested 2014) at Ryukoku University.
Yumiko Ishihama is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Waseda University (~1980–1989) and later held a post there (~1996).

Yun Ji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD in Chinese literature from Fudan University in 2006. He served as a librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).

Yun-hua Jan was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Tan Yun-shan. He was a research fellow at Visva-Bharati University in 1953 and later served as a professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).
Yungfen Ma is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Columbia University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Chün-fang Yü (attested 2011).

Yuri Levada studied philosophy at Moscow University (~1947–1952). He held posts at Moscow State University, the Institute of Sociology, the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences, VTSIOM (~1988–2003), and the Levada Center (~2003–2006).
Yuri Mikhailovich Parfionovich was a Tibetologist who studied under George de Roerich and traditional teacher Bidia Dandaron.
Yusen Kashiwahara was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Otani University (~1937–1940) and later served there as a professor (~1952–1987).

Yusho Miyasaka was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Chisan College and Tohoku University under Shoko Watanabe. He held professorships at Koyasan University and Nagoya University, where he became professor emeritus, and led Chisan Denpōin.

Yusho Wakahara is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami. He lectured at Hanazono University (attested 1987) and served as associate professor (attested 1987–1999) and professor (attested 2011–2013) at Ryukoku University.
Yutai Ikeda was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Otani University and Doho University, where he served as emeritus professor (attested 2006).

Yutaka Hirata was a scholar of Buddhist studies and art history/archaeology who earned his doctorate from Kyushu University. He worked at the Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties, Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University, and Kyushu University, where he became professor emeritus.
